Based on the aforequoted provisions of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-15, there are two (2) steps involved in the issuance of a development permit, namely, (1) the evaluation and approval (non-approval) by the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan on the application; and (2) final review by the City/Municipal Mayor of the application. Under Section 6 (e) of EO 45, local government units are given 30 days only within which to issue development permits. May we note that the aforesaid 30- day period encompasses both the two (2) steps mentioned in the immediately preceding paragraph, not either of the two. This 30-day period was reiterated under DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-15 when it divided into four (4) weeks the processing of the application for development permits. With regard to the first step involved in the issuance of a development permit, we concur with your vievv that EO 45 failed to categorically provide a period within which the sangguniang panlungsod/bayan shall accomplish its evaluation and approval (non-approval) of the application for development permit. Such absence however should not defeat public trust. Item 3.3 of the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-15 categorically provides that the Sanggunian concerned shall approve (disapprove) the application, through a resolution, on the third week. furthermore, a recent law, Republic Act 9485, otherwise known as the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007, mandates public officials to act on matters presented before them in no case shall be longer than five (5) working days in the case of simple transactions and ten (10) working days in the case of complex transactions from the time the request or application was received. Therefore, we are of the belief that the 5 or 10-day period provided for under RA 9485 may be analogously applied to determine the number of days within which for the sanggunian to act on the application for development permit. With regard to the second step involved in the issuance of a development permit, Item 3.4 of the DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-15 provides that if the City/Municipal Mayor does not take action within the prescribed period, either by approving or disapproving the same, such non-action shall mean approval of application. This approval due to the inaction by the City/Municipal Mayor shall be certified by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, through the Provincial Secretary, or in case of the inaction by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan, the DILG Regional Director. We again concur with your observation that the motu proprio approval of the application for development permit is proper only in case of non-action by the City/Municipal Mayor, not due to the inaction by the Sanggunian. Hence, if the delay in the approval or issuance of the development permit is brought about by the Sanggunian concerned, like in the case at hand, the application shall not, after the lapse of 30 days under EO 45, be considered deemed approved. The proper remedies in such situation are either of the following: (1) the applicant may, unless expressly prohibited by law, submit an affidavit, with

supporting technical studies and documents by competent individuals, in lieu of the permit in accordance with Section 5 of EO 45; or (2) the applicant may seek for the intercession of the Provincial Governor in the exercise of the latter's duty to monitor compliance by component cities to EO 45 under Item 4 (A) of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2002-15. We hope we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, uVu-V. JESU B DOQU Dire or III Copy furnished: VICKY P.
